readout_other: Plasma TNF-alpha ELISA; quantitative real-time PCR of spleen proinflammatory cytokine and M1 macrophage marker mRNA
direction_notes: Abdominal ultrasound produced a robust increase in cervical vagus nerve compound activity (excitatory afferent activation), which was associated with downstream anti-inflammatory effects (suppressed plasma TNF-alpha and proinflammatory cytokine expression).

target.label: abdominal ultrasound activating afferent vagus nerve fibers

timing.protocol_description: C57BL/6J mice were subjected to 10 min of abdominal ultrasound stimulation (Burst Mode, 14 MHz), followed by intraperitoneal injection of LPS (15 mg/kg), and then an additional 10 min of ultrasound stimulation. Detailed experimental methods (including full parameters and animal numbers) are provided in the SI Appendix, which was not available for extraction.

flags.reason: 14 MHz is a diagnostic-imaging-range frequency, unusually high compared with typical TUS neuromodulation studies (hundreds of kHz to low MHz); verify this is not a typo.

the paper only states the device setting 'Burst Mode' without giving pulse duration, PRF, or duty cycle, so the underlying pulsing scheme is unknown; classified as pulsed based on the device mode name alone.

the exact sonicated anatomical site (e.g., spleen vs. general abdomen) is not explicitly stated in the main text; target chosen based on the paper's framing that abdominal ultrasound activates afferent vagus nerve fibers.
experimental methods, including animal group sizes, are stated to be in the SI Appendix, which was not available for extraction; main text gives no numeric N.
no device manufacturer or model is given in the main text (methods are in SI Appendix).
